_about: Parameters of the behaviour model (agentcake/detect/model.py and timeline.py). Values are our own research code's, unchanged: the lab's rules and HMM (the behaviour lab's labcore.py, 2026-11-11), the session fallback (cake-data/compare_models.py active_rate and choudhary, 2026-11-11), the missing-data variant from our study of PostHog replays and its decision rule (cake-ph-eval/phcore.py rules_hmm and all_models, 2026-11-12), and cake 0.3.4's per-action judge (its cake.py: rr_actions, p_agent, hmm_smooth; tests/judge_0_3_4.py).

rules._about: The lab's readable rules, scored on each action segment's 25 features (features.py). A rule fires when all of its conditions hold; a segment's score is the logistic of the sum of the weights that fired, so a segment where nothing fires scores 0.5 (no evidence). A condition is [feature, operator, value] or [feature, operator, value, value used when the feature has no data]; without the fourth element, a feature with no data never fires the rule (the missing-data variant). Listed in the lab's order (the order of the sum and of the reasons). The even-typing rule was changed after agent-detector's: the lab fired it from 3 keys, which 20 of 72 three-key stretches of motion-attestation's real typing would trip; it now needs 9 keys at the lab's spread (< 0.15; agent-detector's uniform typing, 8 gaps, uses the same) or, over 3 to 8 keys, a spread under 0.08 (bot-signal's linear typing and motion-attestation's flight times use 0.08), the two never together; the feature key_iv_cv is still measured from 3 keys, as the lab did. Measured: the clean humans' typing segments it fires on went from 9 (in 6 of 11 sessions) to 5 (4 of 11), and every lab agent segment fires as before. kind: the kind of evidence a rule is, for the session's corroboration (session.corroboration).

list.why: very even typing over a few keys
acting while page has no focus

hmm._about: Two-state hidden Markov smoothing of the segment scores over the session (labcore.forward_backward): switch is the chance that the actor changes between two segments, prior the chance the first segment is an agent's, temper flattens the scores (segments are not independent), clamp keeps scores away from 0 and 1.

labels._about: A smoothed segment is an agent's at agent_min or above, a human's at human_max or below, and unsure in between. agent_min is the missing-data variant's threshold: a segment without evidence (0.5) never counts as an agent's.

session._about: The whole session is an agent's when at least min_agent_actions of its action segments are an agent's on their own evidence (labelled agent and an agent rule fired in them: the smoothing labels a strong action's neighbours too, and one action must never make an agent of a session; the minimum verdict.json mixed.min_actions asks of either side), or when the fallback fires; otherwise a human's when any of its segments is; and unsure (shown as a human with thin evidence) when none is either. Segments nobody can tell count for neither side, whatever their share (human + unknown is human, agent + unknown is agent, human + agent + unknown is agent). corroboration (agent-detector's and HABITS' rule): without hard evidence (a rule of hard_rules fired), an agent verdict needs evidence of min_kinds independent kinds (each rule's kind; the fallback's in fallback.kinds); a recording without raw input (rrweb only) can show two kinds at most, so there evidence on min_observations_without_raw_input actions (segments where an agent rule fired, and the session's pointer movement when the active move rate fired; a teleport click lies in a click segment already counted) stands in for the second kind. Otherwise the verdict is unsure and the evidence names the one kind it saw.

fallback._about: Session-level checks that need no rule to fire (Choudhary et al.'s mouse-event rate, as our study of PostHog replays coded it). Active move rate: mousemoves per second counted only inside movement bursts (two moves less than burst_gap_ms apart belong to one burst; min_active_s is the shortest burst time divided into; moves that never form a burst give 0; fewer than min_moves moves give no rate at all, no evidence: after agent-detector's "missing is not negative"); an agent below active_rate_below. Teleport clicks: a click with no mousemove before it, or whose last move came at most click_window_ms before it after a jump of more than jump_px in less than jump_ms; an agent above teleport_share_above. Only a mouse's clicks that show an approach of their own count, on both sides of the share: a click that repeats the previous one in place (features.json double_click_box_px) came with no movement at all. Typing cadence (raw input only): the class isHumanCadence gives the session's typing ends at bot (the cadence section).

cadence._about: Typing cadence (agentcake/detect/cadence.py; a lead from our bench of open-source detectors): isHumanCadence 1.5.1's score and class of a session's typing (github.com/RoloBits/isHumanCadence, commit 21b39ea3, MIT; THIRD_PARTY.md), every value its own, unchanged: weights from analyzer.ts DEFAULT_WEIGHTS, classes from index.ts DEFAULT_CLASSIFICATION_THRESHOLDS, the rest from analyzer.ts, anti-spoof.ts and observer.ts; window and min_samples are index.ts's DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIZE and DEFAULT_MIN_SAMPLES; fine_clock_ms is ours (the earlier key-hold attempt's: a coarse clock gives no evidence). neutral: a measure's score without enough samples. Measured with agentcake eval: on the lab it ends at bot for the four Claude in Chrome sessions and three of the ten human-like Playwright scripts; the recorder's eight people who typed 20 keys or more end at human, their lowest score 0.49; the CMU keystroke benchmark's 408 sittings of 51 people (Killourhy and Maxion 2009) never reach bot, their lowest score 0.356.

arrival._about: Fast arrivals (agentcake/detect/arrival.py; raw input and a mouse only): how many of a session's aimed movements (the path before a press) arrive at their target without slowing down. A path is put on a grid_ms grid; its end share is the mean step over its last end_part of steps over its largest step, and it arrives fast at fast_end_share or more; the check holds when at least min_fast movements arrive fast and they are at least fast_share_at_least of all (fewer than min_fast movements: no evidence). A hand slows down into a target: the public human data sets' median movement ends at 7% (PSAI) to 16% (CaptchaSolve30k) of its top speed; ghost-cursor's path, traced point after point, and windMouse arrive at full speed. Chosen on the public human data sets and human-imitating automation recorded on our test shop, held out by generator: the values no person's session reaches, nor at one step looser in min_fast or in the share, that hold on the most sessions of the other generators. Measured with agentcake eval: no person holds it, nor at one step looser: 0 of the 96 people with 8 aimed movements or more, of 740 (PSAI 509, CaptchaSolve30k 220, the recorder's 11); held out by generator, 8 of 10 ghost-cursor and 8 of 10 motion-attestation sessions, none of Camoufox's eased paths. One kind of evidence (approach): alone it makes an unsure verdict. The run of movements that exceeds the share the most (a fast one counts 1 - fast_share_at_least, any other -fast_share_at_least) goes to the agent on the timeline, from its first move to its last click: one fast arrival is no evidence, people's movements arrive fast 16% of the time (487 of 3,042).

timeline._about: Who did each action, the shares and the hand-offs: cake 0.3.4's per-action judge (tests/judge_0_3_4.py), ported to the raw-event format. An action is a click or an input; inputs less than input_merge_ms apart are one action. Features per action: moves_per_s (mousemoves since the previous action per second, the time at least min_span_s), moves_before_act (mousemoves in the window_ms before it), straight (end-to-end distance over path length of those moves, 1 below min_straight_moves moves), pause_s (seconds since the previous action), no_move_act (1 when at most one move came before it); each capped at caps. p_agent is the logistic of bias plus the weighted features, smoothed by the HMM below and labelled with labels. A run starts at the first event of its actor's first step: for a person, their pointer approach, events at most approach_pause_ms apart (features.json uses the same pause to end an approach). A hand-off is the new actor's first action from the new side's start on, an action as agentcake/data/actions.json defines one for the whole of AgentCake (a click, a key or typed input, a wheel, a scroll the visitor's own input caused; moving the pointer is none), and a run with none hands nothing over; the splices' truth (agentcake/evaluation/splice.py) counts the same events. Between two runs of different actors, the steps the smoothing left unsure go to the side their own scores make likeliest (timeline.handoffs: the maximum-likelihood point of one change, Hinkley 1970), with no parameter of its own; logit_limit bounds a score's log-odds there as in p_agent.

evidence._about: With movement_evidence (above), stretches that are not actions enter the timeline's smoothing when they carry evidence (model.py): action segments of these kinds, scored by the rules above, plus pointer_glides when the pointer glides like a hand (its moves inside movement bursts come at least at the fallback's active_rate_below a second). pointer_glides_weight is the lab's weight for >=10 moves before a click (many_moves_before_click), the same evidence in movement. no_pointer_no_evidence (above): an action with no pointer position in its window gets no evidence from no_move_act and straight, nor does a click that repeats the previous one in place (features.json double_click_box_px: its window holds the previous click's approach and the hand's jitter at most). With both switches false the timeline is 0.3.4's per-action judge, as in the behaviour model's first version.

indicator_tail._about: An agent product's indicator stays lit for a while after the agent's last action: Claude in Chrome takes all its working marks down at once, and only when its turn is over (from its side panel, when its last message is written; driven by Claude Code over MCP, 20 s after its last tool call unless told sooner). Measured on recordings of Claude in Chrome 1.0.107 working alone (19 from its side panel, 20 driven by Claude Code; the recorder's indicator check, the actions as data/actions.json defines them): the time from the agent's last action to its indicator going off was 4.91, 5.00, 5.49, 6.15, 7.12, 11.90, 15.57 and 21.63 s over the 8 turn ends seen from the side panel; driven by Claude Code, every tab was closed while the indicator was still lit, 2.05 to 6.67 s after the last action. So in the last ms of a span that ended with its mark going away while its page view went on (markers.turn_spans' went_off), the agent never acted: when the visitor acted after that span and before any indicator lit again, the steps in those ms are judged on their own evidence, smoothed with the steps that follow, as outside any span (timeline.build). ms gives each product's shortest measured gap (Claude in Chrome's 4.91 s, rounded down); a product with none measured keeps its whole span. Driven by Claude Code, the indicator stays lit longer, and the steps of its tail before these ms still go to the agent.
